transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-approval huddle. As you know, the district's middle-school mathematics assessment is scheduled for May 14, 2027, and I've asked each of you to review the draft administration plan before I give it final approval. The plan currently calls for digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students testing together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout the assessment, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. I'd like to go through each component systematically. Could each of you share your review findings, starting with any concerns you've identified?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Dr. Morris, I need to flag a critical concern with the room assignment in the draft plan. My finalized roster does have 26 students, but the state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students maximum. Because of that limit, I've already prepared Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for the remaining 12 students. However, I should note that this updated two-room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker, so the draft you're reviewing still shows all 26 students in Room 201. We'll need to correct that before approval.

transcript.text: Thank you all for your thorough reviews. Let me summarize the four concerns that have been raised before I make my decision: First, Mr. Bell, the room capacity — the state manual limits testing rooms to 14 students maximum, so we need to split the 26 students across two rooms, 14 in Room 201 and 12 in Room 202. Second, Ms. Shah, the calculator policy — the state manual restricts calculators to section 2 only, and they must be four-function calculators, not graphing calculators. Third, Mr. Nguyen, the testing mode — the tablets cannot run the secure testing application, and the vendor has authorized paper booklets as an alternative, so we need to switch to paper-based testing. Fourth, Ms. Delgado, the storage — completed materials must be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days, not in the general records cabinet. I also want to address the proctor count. If we're now splitting students across two rooms, we'll need a second proctor — one per room. Before I finalize the revised plan, does anyone have any additional concerns or objections to these corrections?
